changes.title: Links open your browser again
changes.body: Report a bug, suggest an improvement, or open an item on warframe.market from the Linux AppImage.

changes.title: Choose what you want to keep
changes.body: Set aside copies or save the parts for a set you are building. Your selling and ducat suggestions take those choices into account.

changes.title: Plan sales for complete sets
changes.body: Add complete sets to Trade Session without counting their parts again in another sale.

changes.title: Find buyers for larger stacks
changes.body: See how much of your stack the listed buyers want, and compare their offers with your asking price.

changes.title: Your latest inventory stays in view
changes.body: An older calculation finishing late will no longer replace your newer scan, import, or plan.

changes.title: More reliable inventory scans
changes.body: Fixed a scan error caused by game data that was not needed to read your inventory.

changes.title: Updates work when you have missed a release
changes.body: Older update links keep working after a newer version comes out.

changes.title: Get protected estimates before connecting WFM
changes.body: Scan or restore inventory to see estimated selling and ducat opportunities that honor your keep rules. The new What I’m keeping summary makes quantities and item rules easier to review.

changes.title: Post only from the inventory you reviewed
changes.body: Listing changes and recovered batches now require the matching current game scan. If your inventory changed, TennoWorth keeps your edits and tells you whether to scan or recheck quantities.

changes.title: Keep your last good inventory after a scan problem
changes.body: Failed scans and scans with no tradeable items leave the last successful inventory visible with its real age. Retry, update, Settings, and reporting actions remain available.

changes.title: Choose whether to share a daily installation count
changes.body: Sharing is off by default. If enabled in Settings, TennoWorth sends a rotating daily token without account, inventory, hardware, version, or activity details.

changes.title: Read what changed after an update
changes.body: TennoWorth brings together the bundled notes for every release you skipped and lets you reopen them from Settings → Updates → What’s new.

changes.title: Tick off what you have already done
changes.body: Routines is a real checklist now: mark a daily or weekly task as you finish it, and the tick stays until that period resets.

changes.title: Keep a list of monthly goals
changes.body: Add as many goals as you are genuinely working on, rename one in place, or remove it. Each goal carries its own tick, and the ticks reset with the month while the goals stay.

changes.title: Put the list in the order you want
changes.body: Move a goal with the Up and Down buttons, or drag it by the handle to any position. The order is kept between sessions.

changes.title: Steadier inventory scanning
changes.body: Capture rejects values that do not match the shape the game produces, keeps session details out of error messages, and bounds its own resource use.

changes.title: Updated the library that secures market connections
changes.body: TennoWorth now uses a rustls release that rejects TLS 1.3 handshake messages sent at the wrong encryption level.

changes.title: Prime parts are no longer missing from what you own
changes.body: Unbuilt prime parts are filed under a Blueprint path that TennoWorth did not recognise, so they were dropped from the owned inventory - one real inventory was short nine parts and 590 ducats. They now resolve, and they count again in the sell view, in set planning and in the Baro ducat total.

changes.title: The comparables drawer accounts for its sample
changes.body: It reports how many asks are in the sample, how many carry a listing time, the newest-to-oldest span, and the seller-status counts; each auction says how long ago it was listed; and the DE band note says plainly that its number is a sold count. A single Refresh replaces keeping the first fetch for the life of the view.

changes.title: A re-checked quote stops looking fresher than it is
changes.body: A cached buyer read was stamped with the clock at the moment it was served instead of when the payload was decoded, so re-checking inside the cache window moved the check time forward while the data stayed the same. The displayed check time now reflects when the quote was actually observed.

changes.title: No more inventory-ready popup after every scan
changes.body: The post-scan pass still rebuilds the tray and records its summary, but it no longer writes an inbox entry or fires a desktop notice that duplicated the daily sell digest. The retired notification category is gone from settings, and stored preferences and inbox rows are cleaned up when they are read.

changes.title: Scan automatically while the game is running
changes.body: An opt-in setting scans every 15, 30 or 60 minutes, only while Warframe is running. A freshly launched game is given time to finish logging in first, failures are shown in Settings instead of as notifications, and nothing changes for anyone who leaves it off.

changes.title: New Prime Access items resolve on day one
changes.body: Items warframe.market lists before the community item data catches up - such as Citrine, Steflos and Corufell Prime - now resolve in inventory, with their set breakdowns and relic rewards.

changes.title: Sell starts with the columns that decide a sale
changes.body: The default preset shows ownership, score, price, trend, volume, advice and potential without scrolling sideways, and a Columns menu adds or removes any column per preset. The first run leads with the scan button.

changes.title: Order changes are reported only when confirmed
changes.body: A repricing, quantity change or visibility change that warframe.market did not confirm is now reported as unconfirmed instead of as done, and an interrupted batch whose outcome is unknown can always be reviewed or discarded.

changes.title: A listed prime set is no longer called unowned
changes.body: A scan never reports a set itself, so the orders panel read a listed set as not owned and offered to delete it. It no longer does, and deleting a listing from the health fixes now asks for a second click.

changes.title: A trade the ledger could not save is retried
changes.body: A confirmed trade that failed to record was lost for good. The log reader now holds its place until the trade is saved and offers it again, without recording it twice.

changes.title: Logging out always wins
changes.body: A logout that landed while the app was still unlocking or signing in could be undone, leaving the app signed in. Logout now takes precedence, and a new sign-in is no longer lost when a silent unlock fails.

changes.title: A quieter, more readable interface
changes.body: Each view leads with its title, prices and trend lines are drawn to be read first, status tags share one style, light-mode text is darker, and stale market data is flagged as a caution rather than an error.

changes.title: Prices never step backwards to an older snapshot
changes.body: The app refuses a downloaded market snapshot older than the one it already holds, so the tray and the dashboard stay on the same, newest prices.

changes.title: Sign in to warframe.market again
changes.body: Signing in opens warframe.market's own page in a private window, and the app never sees your password. On Linux systems where that window cannot display the page, the app asks you to sign in with your browser and paste the session token instead. Saved logins keep working.

changes.title: A rejected update says what to do
changes.body: If an update ever fails its signature check, the app now tells you to download the latest release once, instead of showing the updater's raw error.

changes.title: A listed set is no longer called unowned while prices load
changes.body: Before the market data finished loading, a listed prime set could briefly read as not in your inventory and be offered for deletion. The app now waits for the market data before judging it.

changes.title: Scan problems are reported accurately
changes.body: A report now names the real cause of a failed scan, such as Warframe not running, the game session not found in memory, or the inventory request being refused along with its HTTP status. It no longer reports a connection problem for all of them.

changes.title: Report a sign-in problem from the sign-in window
changes.body: When signing in to warframe.market or unlocking your login fails, the window offers Report a bug. The report records the kind of failure, not its message. A wrong passphrase is not treated as a bug.

changes.title: See what a report includes before sending it
changes.body: The feedback window lists the problems a bug report will carry, such as a failed scan, automatic scan or update, in plain words.

changes.title: The app version is easy to find
changes.body: The bottom of the sidebar now shows the version next to the build, and bug reports fill it in even when the update check has not answered.
